questions.question: You're transferred to a second support person, who asks for your account number again. What went wrong?
options: What the first person learned didn't travel with the transfer
questions.explanation: Agents fail the same way when a handoff carries too little.

questions.question: How is a handoff different from delegating to a worker in orchestrator-worker?
options: The receiving agent takes over the conversation with the user; control doesn't automatically return
questions.explanation: Workers report back; a handoff passes the conversation on.

questions.question: In the summary run, why did the tech agent ask for the app version even though the user had given it?
options: The previous agent's summary left it out, and the tech agent saw only the summary
questions.explanation: Whatever a summary omits is gone for the next agent.

questions.question: With 15 earlier small-talk turns, why did full-history specialists read over five times more?
options: Full history carries every earlier turn, relevant or not, to every agent that takes over
questions.explanation: Full history grows with the conversation; a payload doesn't.

questions.question: Billing and tech keep transferring an 'invoice page error' to each other. What should the system do?
options: Let them continue until one accepts
Detect the ping-pong and escalate to a human with the history
questions.explanation: Guards turn an endless loop into one clear escalation.

questions.question: What's the main cost of the structured-payload policy?
options: You have to design the schema, and facts outside it are lost
questions.explanation: It's complete for what you planned for, and blind to what you didn't.
